newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan profit growth to slow in 98/99 - New Japan Sec.
newsitem.headline: Japan profit growth to slow in 98/99 - New Japan Sec.

text.p: Parent current profits at Japan's major companies are expected to rise by an average of 9.7 percent in the year to March 1998, but the growth rate is expected to slow to 6.0 percent in 1998/99, New Japan Securities Co Ltd said on Thursday.
Based on a survey of 318 major firms listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, excluding financial institutions, the brokerage said the companies are likely to see parent sales rise 2.6 percent in 1997/98.
Manufacturers' current profits are expected to rise 11.2 percent in the current fiscal year, while profit growth at non-manufacturers is forecast to increase 6.1 percent.
The automakers' current profits are expected to rise 21.6 percent, buoyed by the introduction of new models and cost-cutting efforts, the brokerage said.
In 1998/99, sales growth on a parent basis at the companies surveyed is likely to remain steady at an average of 2.6 percent, it said.
Parent current profit growth, however, is expected to decline to 6.0 percent as the firms are expected to derive fewer benefits from a weaker yen.
The brokerage also predicted that steel makers' profits will decline by 14.7 percent in 1998/99 due to a fall in domestic demand and a rise in production capacity at overseas competitors.
